angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 863,364 km at 160.67 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.2240 +/- 0.0223 mas (same row, RUWE 1.16): 160.67 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.241 +/- 0.032 solar radii from Fairnington et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-5126 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.527.8768F/abstract): 863,364 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.24 +/- 0.05 solar masses from Fairnington et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-5126 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.527.8768F/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6150 +/- 110 K from Fairnington et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5126 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.527.8768F/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Fairnington et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5126 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.527.8768F/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-5126.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.344, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-5126 (pscomppars): spectral type F V, from Fairnington et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.527.8768F/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, BD+19 2299: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-5126 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.18 dex, from Fairnington et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.527.8768F/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-5126 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.29885, from Fairnington et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.527.8768F/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-5126 (pscomppars): age 0.8 Gyr, from Fairnington et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024MNRAS.527.8768F/abstract)
